optional: average per teaching period;classroom register;K-6;student stations;large group non-academic instruction;special education classes governed by law
provision: Art. 8-1.1: "Class size shall not exceed an average of 26 students enrolled on a teacher's classroom register per teaching period each school day provided that no teaching period shall have in excess of 29 students." No level-specific elementary cap is stated; 8-1.4 confirms the Article 8 maximum applies "at the elementary level (K-6)." Exceptions: large-group non-academic instruction, individual teacher agreement, and special education classes governed by law; 8-1.2 caps station-based rooms at the number of student stations.

provision: Art. 8-1.3 and 8-1.4 pay elementary special education and Art/Music/Library teachers for overages under "the Cenerini Formula in AAA Case No. 1139-0696-85" (daily gross compensation x number of children in excess of the 8-1.1 maximum / 26); Art. 2 assumes general "class size overage payments" exist and excludes B-9 stipends from them; Art. 2 allows long-term substitutes in-pool to be used "to avert potential class size overages caused by IEP implementation"; Art. 8-1.5 funds a union-selected class-size monitor under the 1986 Superior Court decree.

No employee acceptable-use, email, internet, network or computer-use rules. Vocabularies tried: lexical "internet email computer network acceptable use"; semantic "use of school computers and electronic mail by employees"; and a full read of the technology-adjacent clauses — Art. 8-3.2 (Data Processing: only a Board commitment to "use technology to enhance the operation of the District"), Art. 8-14.5 (bars the employer from using the inter-communication system or electronic devices for observation/evaluation), Art. 16-4.1 (Union officers' use of school telephones and duplication equipment for union business), Art. 11-11 (postings on the district website). None imposes usage rules on employees.

optional: dress code;shall not wear shorts;reflect a positive image;established professional ethics and standards;no formal code of ethics document
provision: Art. 8-24 Dress Code is a negotiated standard of conduct/appearance for teachers ("teachers shall not wear shorts, warm-up suits, torn or faded jeans... Teachers shall continue to reflect a positive image to the students and community"); the Art. 15 grievance definition makes conduct "contrary to established professional ethics and standards" grievable; Art. 9-2 obliges a teacher to cooperate in assault investigations and "report all circumstances." There is no separate code-of-ethics document incorporated by reference — judgment call, see report.

optional: good and just cause;progressive discipline;due process;just cause (sick leave abuse);reasonably related to the seriousness
provision: Art. 8-25(1) Fair Discipline Policy: "A teacher may only be disciplined for good and just cause. A teacher shall be entitled to be provided with due process. Any sanction imposed... shall be reasonably related to the seriousness and nature of the offense and the past record of the teacher," with progressive discipline in 8-25(2); Art. 4-5 separately allows discipline "for just cause" for improper sick-leave use.

optional: Termination;Suspension;five (5) business days;statement of the causes or reasons;school board meeting or hearing;Union Representative present;4-7 shall be terminated
provision: Art. 8-25 lists Suspension and Termination among disciplinary measures and sets the procedure: all relevant evidence to the teacher and Union, a "statement of the causes or reasons" and all documents "not fewer than five (5) business days prior to the scheduled [school board] meeting or hearing," a witness list from the teacher, and the right to Union representation; 8-25(4) preserves the board's power to suspend and/or terminate. Art. 4-7 provides that a teacher who exhausts leave and cannot return "shall be terminated."

optional: annual (non-tenured);scheduled basis (tenured);Teacher Evaluation Committee;Teacher Evaluation Handbook;no number of formal observations stated
provision: Art. 8-14 requires all teachers to be evaluated "on a scheduled basis as determined by the Teacher Evaluation Committee"; 8-14.2 requires annual portfolio evaluation of non-tenured teachers by the second week in May and 8-14.3 evaluation of tenured teachers on the Committee's schedule; the actual evaluation procedure is delegated to the Teacher Evaluation Handbook, a separate document. 8-14.4 presupposes observations ("The principal must have observed the teacher and documented his/her observations... provided the teacher with a copy of each observation") but no required number of formal observations appears anywhere.

No observation length or minimum duration is stated. Vocabularies tried: lexical "observation minutes duration formal observation"; semantic queries on observation practice; and a scan of every "minute"/"period" occurrence in the text — all are lunch periods (8-2.2), unassigned periods (8-4.1), announcement windows (8-11), or the 15-/10-minute day extensions (8-5.5, 8-5.6). Art. 8-14 delegates evaluation procedure to the Teacher Evaluation Handbook, which is not reproduced.

No FMLA or family-medical-leave provision. Vocabularies tried: lexical "family medical leave FMLA" and "serious health condition twelve weeks"; semantic "leave to care for a sick family member" and "unpaid leave of absence for child rearing"; plus a full read of Art. 4 (Sick Leave) and Art. 5 (Leaves of Absence). The statute is never cited and no leave is available for a family member's illness — Art. 4-9(d) expressly bars Emergency Sick Leave Bank time to "attend to the illness of a family member," and Art. 5's only family-related leaves are bereavement (5-3) and unpaid parental/adoptive leave (5-12). Art. 17-5 refers to federal laws only generically.

optional: unpaid;no-pay leave;reimburse the Providence School Department for the premiums;one (1) year extendable to two (2);sick leave available for pregnancy disability (4-6)
provision: Art. 5-12 Parental/Adoptive Leave requires the Superintendent to grant maternity or adoption leave of at least one year (extendable to two), but it is unpaid: the teacher is reinstated "with all rights and benefits accorded to a teacher on a no-pay leave" and may retain medical/dental coverage only by reimbursing the School Department for the premiums at group rate. Art. 4-6 makes ordinary accrued sick leave available for pregnancy/childbirth disability, and 5-12 bars a teacher who elects that Article 4 route from also using 5-12 — so no paid parental, bonding or adoption leave exists beyond accrued sick leave.

Weaker/generic: Art. 5-9 tests "required by the United States Government" (p.14), Art. 8-28.3 "applicable federal, state and local laws" (p.37), Art. 8-32 "federal - or state-imposed sanctions" (p.45).

provision: Numerous Rhode Island citations: the Preamble invokes "Rhode Island General Laws 28-9.3-1 et seq., the Arbitration of School Teacher Disputes" (p.1); Art. 6-2 administers assault leave "in accordance with the terms of R.I.G.L. 9-1-31" (p.16); Art. 6-5 cites "Rhode Island General Law 28-33-19" and the Workers' Compensation laws of the State of Rhode Island (p.17); Art. 8-26 governs retirement by "the statutory language pertaining to the System (R.I.G.L. 16-16-1 et seq.)" optional: standard step on the salary schedule;number of years of regular service completed;long-term substitute;Recall Seniority List;5-5.1 appropriate placement on the salary schedule;seniority purposes only after termination;subset only — no general rule for new hires
provision: Art. 2 (Definitions) credits prior in-district service for step placement for a named subset: a per-diem substitute on the 1994/1995 or any earlier Recall Seniority List who becomes a long-term substitute "will be paid the standard step on the salary schedule retroactive to the first day of service as a per-diem substitute during the school year as dictated by the number of years of regular service completed prior to that time" (p.3). Art. 5-5.1 likewise entitles a teacher returning from paid leave to service credit for "appropriate placement on the salary schedule and increments" (p.13), and Art. 2 (p.4) denies a teacher who terminates and later returns credit for prior years "for seniority purposes only." There is no general rule placing a newly hired teacher on a step by years of prior Providence service — judgment call, see report.

Nothing on out-of-state or other-district experience. Vocabularies tried: lexical "out-of-state experience salary placement credit"; semantic "salary step placement for newly hired teacher with previous teaching experience"; and direct reads of Art. 8-6 Hiring of Teachers (Bachelor's degree and Provisional Certificate requirements only), Appendix A-1/A-2/A-3 (bare step, degree-advancement and longevity tables with no placement rules; A-3 longevity in fact requires that 10 of 15 / 15 of 20 / 20 of 25 years be "in Providence"), and Articles 11-12 on postings and transfers. No maximum credit, other-state, or prior-district crediting language exists.
